How to play

Both views share exactly the same vertical scale. Multiple heights at one time produce multiple objects.

Use Erase and drag over part of a drawing to remove it. Undo restores the previous drawing change.

Draw with Freehand, Line, or Point. Press Play or Pause below the graph.

Drag the orange handle below the graph left or right to inspect a particular moment or move backward. Use the Step buttons for smaller changes. The barriers move with time.

Motorcycle: stay between the road edges and reach the finish before the thirty-second timer expires. Potholes and mud slow the bike; steer around them to save time. Rewind restores the bike’s distance and all accumulated delays. Frogger: cross lanes with traffic moving both ways. Start your drawing at the marked starting point. An internal gap or disconnected jump is a foul. At the end of an unfinished path playback simply waits; extend it and press Play. Each new course is randomized and stays fixed through retries and rewind. The road courses show thirty seconds on the same graph width. The orange bottom handle rewinds or advances the entire scene, even past a collision, so you can inspect and revise a few obstacles at a time. Basketball: bounce the ball at least twice, returning it to the player’s hand between bounces and before he gathers for the shot. Keep the ball in the player’s hand as he gathers and jumps, then draw the shot into the moving basket. Discover the timing and heights by playing and rewinding. The graph controls ball height, including after release. Try an example to see a complete shot. Use Speed to slow playback while you inspect a contact. Orange dots on the time line show the heights being played.

A collision stops every object and marks the contact with a red ×. Rewind to inspect or change your drawing. Courses stay fixed until you choose New course.

After the shot is released, the camera follows the ball; the player stays at his shooting spot on the floor and scrolls off left. The hoop enters near the end. Rewinding restores the player, ball, court, and basket to the same moment.

Each height at the same time creates another object. Basketball checks every ball: each must complete two dribbles, return to the hand, and descend through the rim. Choose your own bounce timing and path. The arm reacts to the release and return; the jump begins after two completed dribbles. Carrying the ball for too long while moving is traveling. No particular floor-contact time or location is required. Small misses near the hand, floor, and basket are accepted. Contact with the player’s shoe or leg is allowed. A successful shot finishes with a short swish animation.

Long winding courses · 2026-10-30 · Mouse, trackpad, and touch supported
